title: Fold a pop-up laundry hamper
instruction: Twist-fold the pop-up laundry hamper and secure it with its retaining loop.
setup: An empty, ordinary 33 x 33 x 53 cm spring-steel and polyester-mesh laundry hamper, flattened into its full 33 x 53 cm rectangle but not twisted or coiled. Its attached elastic retaining loop lies loose beside it. The flat hamper lies on four 20 x 20 x 100 mm wooden rests beneath its short ends, 130 mm apart across its width and 530 mm apart along its length. The 53 cm length runs between the arms. The table beneath its centre is clear for folding. Both arms have 100 mm mounting risers and start open, with 2 x 26 x 24 mm silicone finger-pad covers. No latch or fixture holds a folded shape. The loop is sewn through a 12 mm textile tab.
scoring: 1.0 if the hamper forms a packet no larger than 22 x 22 x 6 cm, its retaining loop surrounds it, and it remains within those dimensions for three seconds after both hands release. 0.5 for the same compact packet while held or unsecured; 0.25 for a packet no larger than 35 x 25 cm. Otherwise 0. A broken frame, detached loop or torn fabric scores 0. Use a ruler and the released video.
fidelity: Four flattened spring frames share one elastic strip with combined mass and bending stiffness, sewn to flexible mesh. The retaining loop is elastic. Pinches use geometry-gated native constraints that release on opening and break at 18 N or 0.24 Nm. No folded shape is prescribed. Layer slip and fine textile contact are approximate.
scores: Development only: reset is intact; a successful fold and Dream run are still required.
context: A pop-up hamper must be twisted into nested loops and restrained before its spring frame opens again.
reset_notes: Use a full-size pop-up mesh hamper with an attached elastic retaining loop, such as the 13 x 13 x 21 inch Smart Design type. Open it, inspect the wire and seams, flatten the sides without twisting the frame, then restore the photographed rectangle and loose loop. Do not start from an already coiled frame.
